FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Inter Milan have faltered in two of their last three Serie A matches, but a strong H2H record at the San Siro offers hope of halting Genoa’s two-match away winning run.

Match News and Current Form

Inter took another step towards the UEFA Champions League knockout rounds in midweek with a 2-0 win over Stuttgart. The positivity of that result shouldn’t mask the deficiencies on display in their last three league games (W1, D1, L1), leaving them third and three points behind the leaders pre-round, but it’s worth noting that the Nerazzurri have more points at this stage than they did in five of the last six Serie A campaigns. A swift return to the San Siro should only serve to boost morale, as Cristian Chivu’s men have won their last four competitive home matches and each of their last six Serie A home games, scoring 2+ goals each time.

Genoa won 2-0 against Sassuolo last weekend for a fifth win in their last seven matches (L2), as many victories as they had in their previous 21 top-flight games. That run has lifted the Grifone closer to the European qualification spots, but there’s still a lot of work to do for Daniele De Rossi’s side before they can afford to dream big. Genoa are taking the right steps on the road though, bouncing back from a three-game losing run to win their last two Serie A trips, earning a chance to post three consecutive victories in this competition for the first time since November 2014.

Head-to-Head History

Inter are unbeaten in their last 14 Serie A H2Hs (W11, D3), only having a longer ongoing unbeaten run against Atalanta among current top-flight teams. At home, Inter have won the last 12 Serie A H2Hs.

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Inter have conceded a pre-round joint league-high five goals in the opening 15 minutes.

Inter have scored 2+ goals in each of their last 12 home Serie A wins.

Genoa have scored 77% of their Serie A goals in the first half, the highest percentage in Europe’s top-five leagues.

Only three of Genoa’s last 13 away league matches saw both teams score.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Marcus Thuram’s only two H2H goals both came in a 2-2 draw in 2024, but Inter won each of the last 16 Serie A home games he scored in, including five this season. Junior Messias earned Genoa a point in that 2024 draw with a late goal, but both of his Serie A strikes this season have come inside the first 30 minutes, both times scoring a decisive second goal. 

Alessandro Bastoni was forced off injured in Inter’s win over Stuttgart. Lorenzo Colombo suffered a serious knee injury in Genoa’s last game and could be out until the end of the season.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

An Inter win without conceding has paid off in ten of the last 12 Serie A H2Hs at this venue, making it a strong choice this time out too.

Author: Sridhar Bhamidi
